newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - HP Q4 results.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - HP Q4 results.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co Monday reported financial results for the fourth quarter of fiscal 1996. The following is a copy of the company's results.

PALO ALTO, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Nov. 18, 1996--Hewlett-Packard Company (NYSE: HWP) today reported a 15 percent increase in orders, 12 percent growth in revenue and a 4 percent decline in net earnings for the 1996 fiscal year's fourth quarter, which ended Oct. 31. For the full 1996 fiscal year, net earnings increased 6 percent on revenue growth of 22 percent. Full-year earnings increased 14 percent before the effects of the company's exit from disk-mechanism manufacturing and related operating losses in that business.

Net earnings for the fourth quarter were $648 million, or 62 cents per share, on approximately 1.05 billion shares of common stock and common-stock equivalents outstanding. This compares with net earnings of 64 cents per share on approximately 1.05 billion shares and equivalents outstanding in the fourth quarter of last year, a period in which HP's net earnings rose 42 percent. (All figures for earnings per share (EPS) and number of shares and equivalents outstanding reflect the company's 2-for-1 stock split in July 1996.)

Net revenue for the quarter was $10.1 billion, compared with $9.0 billion for the year-ago period. Net revenue in the United States was $4.7 billion, an increase of 10 percent over last year's fourth quarter, while net revenue from outside the United States rose 14 percent to $5.4 billion.

"We're encouraged by the rebound in order growth this quarter, but somewhat disappointed with our earnings," said Lewis E. Platt, HP chairman, president and chief executive officer. "Our disappointment is tempered by the fact that this was a tough comparison with very strong earnings growth in last year's fourth quarter. Revenue growth fell a bit short, due largely to sluggish order growth in the prior quarter. But we're quite pleased with the substantial reduction in operating-expense growth, which shows that we moved quickly to adapt to changing business conditions."
ORDER SUMMARY

Orders for the quarter were $10.0 billion, an increase of 15 percent over the same period a year ago. U.S. orders grew 10 percent to $4.7 billion, while orders from outside the United States increased 20 percent to $5.3 billion.

In the company's computer business, orders increased 20 percent and totaled $8.2 billion. HP NetServer systems and desktop PCs posted excellent order increases. HP Pavilion multimedia home PCs showed very strong growth, as did PC-networking products, but demand for mobile PCs was weak.

HP 9000 servers posted a good increase, but orders for workstations were weak. HP OpenView, the company's family of products for network and systems management, achieved very good growth this quarter.

Order growth in the company's service and support business was excellent this quarter. Demand for consulting and educational services was strong, and orders for onsite hardware support and multivendor support also increased.

HP LaserJet printers registered moderate overall order growth. HP Color LaserJet 5 printers achieved extraordinary growth and acceptance worldwide, and LaserJet printer supplies continued to post strong growth in all regions. Orders for scanners, especially the low-cost HP ScanJet 4p scanner, were very strong.

Inkjet products achieved very strong order growth, due largely to broad acceptance of the HP DeskJet 870C printer and the newly introduced DeskJet 690 photo-quality color printer. Inkjet printer supplies registered outstanding order growth.

Orders in the test-and-measurement business declined 1 percent, compared with a very strong year-ago quarter. Demand for acceSS7, a system that gathers real-time data on telecommunications network activity, was outstanding, and communications-test equipment showed strong growth. Semiconductor-test equipment orders declined compared with last year, reflecting a slowdown in the growth of semiconductor manufacturing capacity.

In the company's medical-products group, orders also declined 1 percent, compared with last year's outstanding fourth quarter. Orders in the chemical-analysis business increased 2 percent, compared with the year-ago quarter, and orders for electronic components declined 11 percent.
COSTS AND EXPENSES

Cost of goods sold this quarter was 67.2 percent of net revenue, compared with 65.3 percent in the year-ago period and 68.0 percent in the third quarter of fiscal 1996. (Without the impact of the company's costs associated with the exit from disk-mechanism manufacturing and related operating losses in that business, cost of goods sold would have been 66.0 percent of net revenue in the third quarter and 66.8 percent in the fourth quarter.) Pricing pressures, the mix of products that comprised revenue, and slow growth in some product lines were the major factors in this quarter's increase in cost of sales.

Operating expenses increased 11 percent, compared with the same quarter last year, following growth rates of 15 percent in the third quarter and 23 percent in the second quarter. Operating expenses this quarter were 24.1 percent of revenue, compared with 24.3 percent in the year-ago quarter and 25.3 percent in the third quarter of this year.
"We're pleased with the significant progress we've made on operating expenses," said Platt. "Our businesses moved quickly to slow hiring and reduce other discretionary expenses."
ASSET MANAGEMENT

As a percentage of net revenue, accounts receivable was 18.5 percent, compared with 21.4 percent in the year-ago quarter and with 17.5 percent in the third quarter. Net property, plant and equipment was 14.4 percent of net revenue, compared with 14.9 percent a year ago and with 14.0 percent last quarter. Inventory was 16.7 percent of net revenue, compared with 19.1 percent in the same period last year and with 18.5 percent in the prior quarter.

"Asset management was excellent this quarter," said Platt. "We've been working to get inventory into better balance, and we achieved real progress across our businesses. Inventory management will remain a high priority in the months ahead."
YEAR-END REVIEW

For fiscal 1996, net earnings totaled $2.6 billion, an increase of 6 percent, compared with the $2.4 billion the company earned in fiscal 1995. Net earnings per share totaled $2.46, an increase of 6 percent over the $2.31 (restated to reflect the July 1996 2-for-1 stock split) earned in fiscal 1995.

Orders for fiscal 1996 were $38.9 billion, an increase of 19 percent over last year. U.S. orders totaled $17.2 billion, an increase of 17 percent, while orders from outside the United States were $21.7 billion, up 21 percent over last year.

Net revenue increased 22 percent to $38.4 billion, compared with $31.5 billion in fiscal 1995. Net revenue in the United States was $17.0 billion, an increase of 22 percent over the previous year, while net revenue from outside the United States increased 22 percent to $21.4 billion.
BUSINESS OUTLOOK

"Our results for the year were good, especially in the first half," said Platt. "The second half fell short of our goals. However, we're encouraged by an improved order growth rate in the fourth quarter and by the steady improvement in our expense structures through the year. In addition, we've made progress on inventory issues, and most of the profit impact of our decision to exit disk-mechanism manufacturing is now behind us.

"As we begin the new fiscal year, we see many opportunities across our businesses. We have innovative technologies, ambitious product programs and strong channel partnerships. We will continue to make appropriate investments in all these areas.

"At the same time, we're refining our strategies in some businesses where growth has been slow, and there won't be any letup in our efforts to improve our cost structures across the company. We are ready for the intense competition, difficult pricing environment and economic uncertainty we expect to see in the months ahead. Our businesses are fundamentally strong, and we are well-positioned to succeed."

Hewlett-Packard Company is a leading global manufacturer of computing, communications and measurement products and services recognized for excellence in quality and support. HP has 112,000 employees and had revenue of $38.4 billion in its 1996 fiscal year.

This news release contains forward-looking statements, based on current expectations, that involve risks and uncertainties that could cause HP's results to differ materially. In addition to the factors discussed above, other risks include the timely development, production and acceptance of new products and services and their feature sets; the challenge of managing asset levels, including inventory; the flow of products into third-party distribution channels; and the other risks detailed from time to time in the company's Securities and Exchange Commission reports, including, but not limited to, the report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 31, 1996.
Current and historical financial information now is available at HP's Financial Online site on the World Wide Web. Address: http://www.hp.com/go/financials

In fiscal 1996, the company changed its order-reporting policies for its support businesses to report orders when received instead of as services are provided. Fiscal 1995 orders have been restated to reflect this change, which did not have a material impact on order-growth rates. -0-
